scope: Theorem 8.6 (Exclusion of vanishing profiles at individual centers) of the manuscript “Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar” (preprints/Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fefc18481d52acb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 90. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider sequences of levels kn → ∞, scales dn = e−kn , and amplitudes Bn = µ(kn) → ∞. Suppose there are envelopes Nn satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 8.4 with constants independent of n, and Nn(kn) ≤ CBn. For a fixed α ∈ (1/2, 1) and a sufficiently large fixed aperture L, there cannot be centers xn such that, for every fixed c > 0, sup cdn≤δ≤δb |ℜs−xn|≤Lδ δ=H−ℑs dnM(s) Bn  δ dn α −→ 0. (8.35) In particular, suppose the profiles Fn(S) = dn Bn f(xn + iH + dnS), Qn(S) =  dn Bn 2 q(xn + iH + dnS) (8.36) converge to (0, 0) on compact subsets of the lower half-plane. They cannot also satisfy, for some fixed α0 > 1/2 and an aperture L sufficiently large for a chosen exponent 1/2 < α < min(1, α0), dn Bn M(s) ≤ C  dn δ α0 (dn ≤ δ ≤ δb, |ℜs − xn| ≤ Lδ). (8.37) Every compact holomorphic limit of the pair in (8.36) is pure: its product FQ vanishes identically.
